title: Ibrahim and his family
blurb: One family: Ibrahim, Lut, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub and Yusuf. From Iraq to Palestine, Makkah and Egypt.

events.title: The star, the moon, the sun
events.what: Ibrahim watches a star, the moon, then the sun. Each one sets. He turns to the One who made them.

events.title: Ibrahim pleads with his father
events.what: Ibrahim gently asks his father why he worships what cannot hear or see. Threatened with stoning, he answers 'Peace be upon you' and promises to pray for him.

events.title: Ur falls
events.what: Elamite armies sack Ur and end the last great Sumerian dynasty. Poets mourn the city in the Lament for Ur.
events.tie: The Quran recalls cities that did wrong, now 'fallen into ruin', with their abandoned wells and lofty palaces (22:45).
events.note: Dates this early can shift by decades. Ur's link to Ibrahim comes from the Bible and some commentators.

events.title: Ibrahim breaks the idols
events.what: Ibrahim rejects the idols of his people and his father Azar. He breaks the idols and is thrown into a fire that does not burn him.

events.title: Ibrahim faces the king
events.what: Ibrahim debates the king who claims to give life and death. The king is silenced when told to bring the sun from the west.

events.title: Harran, city of the moon
events.what: Harran in northern Mesopotamia is a centre of moon worship on the trade road west. Tradition says Ibrahim stopped here on his way to Sham.
events.tie: Ibrahim's lesson of the setting star and moon (6:76-77) answers exactly this kind of worship.
events.note: His stay in Harran comes from the Bible and early historians, not the Quran.

events.title: Ibrahim migrates
events.what: Ibrahim and Lut migrate to the land of Sham. Ibrahim settles near Hebron, where he is later buried.

events.title: Ibrahim and Sarah in Egypt
events.what: A tyrant king seizes Sarah, but each time he reaches for her his hand is gripped. He lets her go and gives her Hajar as a servant.

events.title: The four birds
events.what: Ibrahim asks to see how the dead are brought to life, so his heart may be at rest. He places parts of four birds on the hills and calls them. They come flying back.

events.title: The angel guests
events.what: Angels visit Ibrahim as guests. He serves them a roasted calf. They bring news of a son, Ishaq, and of Lut's town.

events.title: Lut leaves by night
events.what: The angels tell Lut to leave with his family in the last part of the night and not look back. His wife stays behind and is lost with the town.

events.title: The towns of Lut
events.what: Lut's people reject him. Angels visit, the town is turned upside down and stones rain on it.

events.title: Hajar, Ismail and Zamzam
events.what: Ibrahim leaves Hajar and the infant Ismail in the empty valley of Makkah. Zamzam springs from the ground.

events.title: Seven runs between Safa and Marwa
events.what: When the water runs out, Hajar runs seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa looking for help, until Zamzam bursts out. Pilgrims still walk her steps.

events.title: Makkah's first people
events.what: The Arab tribe of Jurhum settles by Zamzam. Ismail grows up among them, learns their Arabic and marries into them.

events.title: Change your threshold
events.what: Ibrahim visits while Ismail is out. One wife complains of hardship, a later one gives thanks. He advises Ismail to part with the first and keep the grateful one.

events.title: The sacrifice
events.what: Ibrahim is told in a dream to sacrifice his son. Both submit. A ram is sent instead. Eid al-Adha remembers this.

events.title: Raising the Kaaba
events.what: Ibrahim and Ismail raise the walls of the Kaaba and call people to Hajj.

events.title: Ishaq and Yaqub
events.what: Ishaq is born to Sarah in old age. His son Yaqub, also called Israil, fathers the twelve tribes.

events.title: Palaces of Crete
events.what: On Crete, the Minoans build the palace of Knossos and trade by ship across the eastern Mediterranean.
events.tie: The Quran counts 'ships in the sea, like mountains' among Allah's signs (42:32).

events.title: The Indus cities empty
events.what: As rivers shift and rains fail, the great Indus cities slowly empty. Their writing has still not been read.
events.tie: The Quran invites people to travel and reflect on the ruins of those before them (30:42).

events.title: Ibrahim's prayer for Makkah
events.what: In old age Ibrahim prays that Makkah be safe, that his children be kept from idols, and that people's hearts incline towards them. He thanks Allah for Ismail and Ishaq.

events.title: Ibrahim is buried at Hebron
events.what: Ibrahim dies and is buried in a cave at Hebron beside Sarah. The shrine above it, al-Haram al-Ibrahimi, is honoured by Jews, Christians and Muslims.
events.note: The burial place comes from the Bible and early Muslim historians. The Quran does not name it.

events.title: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon
events.what: Young Yusuf dreams that eleven stars, the sun and the moon bow to him. Yaqub tells him to keep it from his brothers.

events.title: Yusuf in the well
events.what: His brothers throw Yusuf into a well. Travellers find him and sell him in Egypt for a few coins.

events.title: Yusuf chooses prison
events.what: Raised in the house of an Egyptian official, Yusuf refuses his master's wife and seeks refuge in Allah. Though innocent, he prefers prison to sin.
events.note: Commentators call her Zulaykha. The Quran does not name her.

events.title: Yusuf in prison
events.what: Two young prisoners ask Yusuf about their dreams. First he teaches them: are many lords better, or Allah, the One?

events.title: The king's dream
events.what: Jailed on a false charge, Yusuf reads the king's dream: seven fat years, seven lean. He is put in charge of Egypt's stores.

events.title: The king's cup
events.what: Yusuf keeps his brother Binyamin by hiding the king's cup in his bag. Yaqub, losing a second son, says: 'I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.'
events.note: The name Binyamin comes from the commentators. The Quran says 'his brother'.

events.title: The family reunited
events.what: Famine drives his brothers to Egypt. Yusuf forgives them. Yaqub's sight returns and the family settles in Egypt.

events.title: Canaanites in the Nile Delta
events.what: Settlers from Canaan and Syria build a thriving town at Avaris in the Nile Delta. Their descendants, the Hyksos, later rule northern Egypt.
events.tie: In Yusuf's story the Quran calls Egypt's ruler 'the king' (12:50), never Pharaoh; some historians place Yusuf in this age.
events.note: When Yusuf lived is debated. Neither the Bible nor archaeology gives an agreed date.

events.title: The patience of Ayyub
events.what: Ayyub loses health, wealth and children, stays patient, and is restored.
